title: Start the system confirms everything is operational within minutes, then fires the queue in order
why: Jason, 2026-11-17: 'the start needs to confirm it's operational within minutes similar to the preflight. Once its operational the queue for firing each is clean and efficient, no need to rush. I just dont want the system acting incorrectly because something wont become active until step 999 or 6 hours later.' 1. A new step, Confirm each workflow and task is operational: every workflow and task is tested like the pre-flight (services, keys, scheduled jobs, gate, a dry run where one exists); the open card looks again every 15 seconds, so it takes minutes; one not operational is held with its answer and fix, retested at each look, and the rest go on. 2. The master comes on once all are tested; then every confirmed workflow switches on in order at once, each new task once its workflow is on; nothing waits for the one before to run. 3. Each one on is watched by itself (start_gate_runs / start_gate_hours, now the watch): a service issue that holds it, out of budget or too many failed runs stops that one alone, with its fixes on the card; the rest carry on. A step stopped by an issue that no longer holds carries on by itself. 4. Each workflow and task opens to Confirmed, Started, Running, Complete, Active status. 5. Thresholds' wording, decisions/0163 §10.2's note, FAQ. 6. A stopped step names the right action ('What to do:'): Check again when its issue no longer holds the service, Check issue now when it still does, Try it again otherwise.

log.msg: Plan approved (no switch: everyone at once when published), advancing on schedule.
